title: My Family
subtitle: Emma's parents, her older sister, her younger brother — and one week in December.
description: An A1 reading and listening text about family words, ages and relationships, including the false friend 'parents'.
source: authored for this site; no source document
lexicalSet: an A1 naming text: the short passage is a frame for the everyday words the glossary teaches
passage: My family is not big. I have one brother and one sister.
My parents live in Ohio, in the same house for thirty years. My father, Dan, is sixty-two. He works in a store. My mother, Laura, is sixty, and she is a nurse. She works at night.
My sister, Kate, is older than me. She is thirty-five, and she has two kids, a son and a daughter. Her husband is a teacher. They live near my parents, so my mother sees the kids every week.
My brother, Nick, is younger. He is twenty-eight and he is not married. He lives in Denver and works for a small company. We talk on the phone every Sunday.
I live far from all of them. But every December we go to Ohio, and for one week the house is full and loud and very warm.

images.alt: A family gathered around a table in a stone-walled room, with children playing on the floor
images.caption: *Le gioie di casa* (The Joys of Home) — Pietro Saltini.

vocabulary.definition: your mother and your father — careful: not all your relatives
a place where you buy things
a person who helps sick people at a hospital
having a husband or a wife

exercises.title: Understanding the Text
exercises.instructions: Read again and choose the best answer.

items.prompt: How many brothers and sisters does Emma have?
options: Two: one brother and one sister
items.explanation: “I have one brother and one sister.”

options: She helps sick people at night
items.explanation: She is a nurse and she works at night.

items.prompt: Who is the oldest of the three children?
items.explanation: Kate is older than Emma, and Nick is younger.

items.prompt: Why does Emma's mother see Kate's children every week?
options: Because Kate lives close to her parents

items.prompt: How often does Emma see her family in Ohio?
options: One week a year, in December
items.explanation: Every December they go for one week. On Sunday she only talks to Nick on the phone.

exercises.title: Family Words
exercises.instructions: Choose the word that matches the meaning.

items.prompt: Your mother and your father are your ___.
items.explanation: Careful: in English, parents means only your mother and father.

items.prompt: Your brother's male child is his ___.
items.explanation: A son is a male child.

items.prompt: Kate is thirty-five and Emma is thirty-two. Kate is ___.
Nick has no wife. He is not ___.
items.explanation: To be married is to have a husband or a wife.

items.prompt: There are twelve people in a small room. The room is ___.
items.explanation: Full means with no empty space.

exercises.title: Who Is Who?
exercises.instructions: Match each person to the right description.

pairs.right: Emma's father. He works in a store.
Emma's mother. She is a nurse and works at night.
Emma's older sister. She has two kids.
Emma's younger brother. He lives in Denver.
Emma's husband. He works from home.

discussion: Do you have brothers or sisters? Are they older or younger?
When do you see your family?
